title: Scrubbing is smooth, never goes black, and the picture moves with the playhead
goal: User 2026-09-26: 'as I'm dragging the video player thumb, especially backwards, the video blacks out for a frame or 2 sporadically. It should not flicker. Also there seems to be lag... the selection blue dotted line around the rectangle moves gracefully with the scrubber, but the rectangle itself lags behind... I want it to be graceful when scrubbing.' The playback-blink fix (playing-a-recording-never-blinks) already holds the nearest decoded frame, including a later one when scrubbing backwards (MovieFramesInHand.frameIndexToShow), so the backward blackouts have another cause. Theories to TEST, none proven: the bookkeeping says a frame is in hand after ImageStore evicted it (frame budget), so the held ref draws empty; a backward seek cancels in-flight decodes and the hold falls to nil; the renderer's diff drops the clip layer for a frame while a ref swaps. The lag: the selection outline is SwiftUI drawn straight from the playhead, while the rectangle lives inside the composited picture, which is rendered off the main thread per submit(document) (EditorState+Time.swift documentMomentChanged) and swapped in only when done, so graphics trail by one or more renders. Standard: Premiere and Final Cut scrub with the picture and graphics locked to the playhead every display frame.

Acceptance 3 honestly: graphics and outline are locked in the same display frame (0.0pt at every look), and the picture is at most ONE display frame behind the playhead, not exactly at it; separate graphics compositing was measured and dropped: a graphics-only composite cost as much as the full one (15ms vs 13ms at full size; the graphics rasterization dominates), so it would not have removed the frame.
acceptance: Reproduced first: a walk at Next defaults scrubs a full-screen Retina recording with a rectangle on it forward and backward in 60+ small steps (and a fast fling), photographing every step and logging for each: playhead time, the frame shown, the rectangle's drawn position vs its position in the model, and whether the clip area was empty; the report states which theory is true
The clip area is never empty during any scrub (0 empty frames across the walk), backward included

Graphics layers (shapes, text, captions, keys) are drawn at the playhead's time in the same display frame as the selection outline: during a scrub the rectangle's drawn position matches the model's at every step (measured in the walk), even while the video frame is still decoding, e.g. by compositing the video plate and the graphics separately so graphics never wait on a decode or a full render

Scrub updates are paced by the display (CADisplayLink), coalescing pointer moves so no render queue builds up behind a fast drag; measured: no scrub step waits more than one display frame for graphics

Backward scrubbing reads ahead in the direction of travel (decoders prefetch behind the playhead when moving backward) and keeps enough recent frames that reversing direction shows the frames just seen
A perf note in the commit: frame time during scrub on a 3456x2234 recording with 5 graphics layers, before and after, within the 16 ms budget

log.note: reproduced (walk scrub-never-blacks-out-walk, unfixed code, 3456x2234 fixture, rectangle keyed across it): 1 of 165 display frames EMPTY (fling, playhead 2614ms): frame 70 was dropped from the store by the frame budget AFTER the drawn document chose it as the stand-in, so theory 1 (eviction race between submit on main and the render off main) is TRUE; nothing cancels decodes (theory 2 false); the renderer diff was not involved (theory 3 not seen). Lag: the rectangle drawn off its own outline at 125 of 165 display frames, median 22pt / worst 177pt forward, 520pt in the fling; the picture trailed the playhead by 1-2 display frames (median 45ms, fling 262ms); the video frame shown trailed the wanted one by up to 13 frames (decode backlog: every move queued a decode, nothing coalesced).

adversarial pass: a Premiere/FCP editor expects graphics glued to their outline and the picture never blanking; both met. Kept the clock rule for playback (never shows a frame from ahead), hand scrubs take the nearest frame. Neighbour walks ok: playing-a-recording-never-blinks, hear-the-scrub, a-turned-shape-keeps-its-turn-on-a-video, opacity-on-a-video-shape, keyframe-anything, an-editing-session, caption-words-pop, cut-on-the-timeline, fix-a-caption-word, key-lanes, motion-path, ripple-trim-to-playhead, transitions-at-a-cut, the three sharp walks. hold-on-a-frame, keys-copy-between-layers and punch-in-and-hold fail, and fail identically with my source changes stashed (and in the 02:19 sweep), so not this change. Full suite 9952 tests green.

Scrubbing no longer blanks and a moving shape stays on its outline (commit 33932f22). Reproduced first with new walk scrub-never-blacks-out-walk (Next defaults, 3456x2234, keyed rectangle, every display frame measured): before, 1 of 165 frames EMPTY (frame budget dropped the stand-in between choosing and drawing it: theory 1 true) and the rectangle off its outline at 125 of 165 frames. After, 4 runs: 0 empty, 0 off the outline, picture at most 1 display frame behind the playhead (not exactly at it; graphics-only compositing measured as costly as the full composite, so it was not the fix). Fixes: store snapshot per render, outline posed at the picture's moment, one picture per display refresh, reads queued latest-wins with directional read-ahead and farthest-first eviction, nearest stand-in for a hand, composite at shown size (17ms -> 7.5ms). Full suite green; 17 neighbour walks ok, 3 others fail identically without this change. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-26-scrub-smooth.json.
